newsitem.title: USA: TransTexas Gas selling subsidiary, hopes to get $1 billion.
newsitem.headline: TransTexas Gas selling subsidiary, hopes to get $1 billion.

text.p: TransTexas Gas Corp. said Wednesday that it was negotiating to sell, for at least $1 billion, its TransTexas Transmission Corp. subsidiary, which owns natural gas producing properties and a 1,100-mile pipeline system.
"This is the highest priority in the company at this time and we are endeavouring to close as quickly as possible," President and Chief Operating Officer Arnold Brackenridge said in a statement.
"Although we cannot discuss the details of the transaction, it is anticipated to result in consideration in excess of $1.1 billion," Brackenridge added.
Houston-based TransTexas said it was in "exclusive negotiations with an unaffiliated third party" for the cash sale of TransTexas Transmission, but it did not identify the potential buyer.

The company said that improved cashflow from other properties outweighed the benefits that could be achieved by extensive capital deployment for further development of TransTexas Transmission's properties.

"Assuming that a transaction can be concluded at a price beneficial to the company, it makes sense to monetize this subsidiary now and focus upon the ongoing growth of our new development areas," Brackenridge said.
Until 1996, the TransTexas Transmission's Lobo Trend property contributed substantially all of TransTexas' natural gas production, with more than 800 wells.
However, since TransTexas' discovery of the new Bob West North field, its dependence upon the Lobo field has been dramatically reduced, the company said.
The Lobo field now accounts for less than half of the company's daily average natural gas equivalent production, it said.
TransTexas Gas, the third-largest producer of natural gas in Texas, is engaged in the exploration, production and transmission of natural gas and oil.
The company's stock added 75 cents to $17 in early trading on the Nasdaq market.
